framing: SCALE COMPARISON, not withdrawal attribution. Prince William data centers are supplied by Prince William Water (Occoquan/Potomac public supply), not by direct withdrawal from these streams. Ratios express how large the local on-site draw is relative to the water moving through the basins the buildings occupy.
buildout_caveat: Draw figures cover ALL buildings in the watershed (built, under construction and planned) -- i.e. a full-buildout condition, not today's operating fleet. Today's completed-only draw is far smaller (see completed_only_* fields).
gage_sensitivity: Flow depends on which gage represents the buildings' position in the basin. Broad Run is bracketed by two gages (Buckland 50.2 sq mi upstream, Bristow 89.6 sq mi downstream) and BOTH ratios are reported rather than assuming one is conservative. Historical (discontinued) records are stationary references; under the current drought (PDSI -5.3, METHODOLOGY 31) actual flows are likely below them, which would make the ratios larger, not smaller.

QUANTICO CREEK.gage: S F Quantico Creek near Independent Hill

data_gaps: POWELLS CREEK (gage 01657895 has ~2 years of record -- insufficient)
headline: Broad Run carries the county's data-center concentration (166 buildings, 50 built today). On an annual-average basis the on-site draw is only 4.22% of the basin's mean flow. But on an ICPRB peak summer day at FULL BUILDOUT it reaches 104.7% of the basin's lowest-month mean flow (95.6% at the downstream gage) -- i.e. of the same order as the entire low flow of the stream the buildings sit on, and in the month that flow is lowest (METHODOLOGY 31). Today's completed fleet is 13.7%. This is a scale comparison, not a withdrawal: the water is supplied from the Occoquan/Potomac system. The binding constraint is peak-day-on-low-flow, not the annual mean.
